sourceState: Mutable, uncommitted working tree. Eight listed rows were reassessed at this refresh; the remaining 190 retain their previous assessment. This is source coverage, not candidate-bound verification or acceptance.

sampling.method: deterministic sha256 ranking; up to six required source outcomes per WP; outcome IDs are the sampling units; no effort weights

limitations: Row-level source coverage is not a percentage of engineering effort, time remaining, or release readiness.
Partial rows receive no fractional implementation credit; their remaining work varies and they may contain substantial code.
The source is changing during assessment; some findings may already be under repair. Corrections to earlier classifications do not imply code loss.
A complete test harness may count as implemented source; this does not mean browser or device acceptance was executed.
No global CODE_COMPLETE_GO has been issued, and acceptance remains not run.
Only eight affected sample rows were refreshed at this timestamp; the other 190 retain their earlier assessments and may be stale.

outcomes.description: Create the ledger named in WP-00 with one row per concrete user-observable capability, format variant, option and backend. Include G01–G55 and every specific item named in WP-01–WP-32.
outcomes.reason: The ledger has 1,901 required rows, but only one row currently has a nonempty backend contract, so the demanded per-backend and per-variant enumeration is not complete.

outcomes.description: Recheck every “not found” or “unverified” row against source, public exports, installed package and existing tests. Merge semantically identical rows; do not infer behavior from names.
outcomes.reason: A bounded source sample and working notes exist, but 1,885 of 1,901 ledger rows remain source-unverified and the required exhaustive source/export/installed-package recheck and semantic merge are not established.

outcomes.description: For each public capability, track the exact package/subpath, backend, version, asset format, browser/OS/device class, known limitations and evidence level in the WP-00 ledger. A capability can be **source-tested**, **browser-tested on software**, **browser-tested on hardware**, **device-tested**, **unsupported**, or **unverified**; do not promote one level into another. Desktop browser-family coverage, mobile browsers, native GPU and physical spatial devices are separate cells. A missing physical device receipt is an explicit acceptance limitation, not a fabricated pass or a blocker to freezing completed source work.
outcomes.reason: The 1,901-row ledger has status and limitation fields, but inspection found only three rows with public entrypoints, one row with backend mappings, and no source-evidence arrays populated; the requested per-capability format/device/evidence cells are incomplete.

outcomes.description: Record each capability, implementation ownership, status, public API, tests, limitations and evidence. WP-00 owns this file for the entire program; WP-18 supplies documentation updates through WP-00.
outcomes.reason: The ledger records stable IDs, ownership, priorities and status fields, but most API and backend mappings are empty and no source evidence array is populated.

outcomes.description: Complete the capability ledger in WP-00; enumerate every public capability and option, map it to an existing implementation or a named work package, and close every row with executable evidence.
outcomes.reason: The ledger enumerates 1,901 required source outcomes with work-package owners, but most lack public entrypoints, all source evidence arrays are empty, and no row is recorded complete with executable evidence.

outcomes.description: Every supported option must produce its documented observable behavior or a stable actionable error. Compile-only success, a counter change, parsing metadata, an opaque canvas, or a mock device alone does not establish a visual or hardware claim.
outcomes.reason: Array and stereo unsupported-depth requests now reach preflight. The universal option contract remains incomplete: camera options are not exhaustively covered by discovery, and lower-level tiled camera resize can use tile rather than full-image aspect.

outcomes.description: Preserve default-origin, disposed batch and typed attribute geometry query correctness. Exclusive execution owner: wp01_geometry. Source verification: tests/unit/engine/scene-queries.test.ts; tests/unit/agent-api/scene-query-mesh.test.ts.
outcomes.reason: Missing transforms use origin, disposed batches are skipped at target collection and raycast, and mesh queries decode shader-facing typed attributes. This classifies the source behavior; no fresh test run is claimed.

outcomes.description: Make merge and deindex operations preserve or explicitly reject every attribute, morph, group, draw range and topology
outcomes.reason: Typed position, normal and tangent morph channels now expand and merge with explicit validation, and incompatible metadata is rejected. However, untyped additional top-level streams such as tangents are ignored by normalization and metadata validation: deindex spreads them unchanged while merge omits them. The broad preserve-or-reject-every-attribute outcome remains incomplete.

outcomes.description: deformed meshes
outcomes.reason: Mesh queries evaluate position morphs and skinning, including extra influences. The CPU query path has no evaluation of arbitrary custom vertex-shader deformation, so broad deformed-mesh picking remains incomplete.

outcomes.description: transform
outcomes.reason: Translate, rotate, and scale gizmo and ray-driven drag operations exist, but the control owns no DOM listeners; callers must provide pointer, touch, keyboard, focus and cancellation routing.

outcomes.description: triangles
outcomes.reason: The public math module provides triangle normal, barycentric containment, box intersection, and closest-point operations.

outcomes.description: Add index, transform, merge, morph, attribute and bounds regressions.
outcomes.reason: The requested regression source covers index widths, computed bounds, affine transforms, morph and custom streams, deindex, and merge. Test execution is not claimed.

outcomes.description: traversal
outcomes.reason: SceneNode.traverse visits the node and recursively traverses a snapshot of its children.

outcomes.description: Assert view isolation, resize, clipping, camera and post behavior using independent fixtures.
outcomes.reason: The test source constructs mock fixtures and asserts independent view clipping, per-view camera culling and post settings, resizing and target cleanup. The ledger reports 99/99 for the orthographic stereo, camera options and viewport source suites; this is source/mock evidence, not browser or device acceptance.

outcomes.description: Define independent viewport/scissor, camera and post settings for array/stereo views.
outcomes.reason: Array entries and stereo eyes expose separate camera, viewport, scissor and post settings and lower them into view records. However, eye camera settings are not fully independent: mixed perspective/orthographic eyes and nonstandard orthographic depth are rejected. Source tests cover supported eye overrides; device acceptance is separate.

outcomes.description: Perspective, orthographic, cube, array and stereo cameras; per-view projection, viewport/scissor, culling, postprocessing and camera controls.
outcomes.reason: Perspective, orthographic, cube, array and stereo authoring and per-view rendering exist; orthographic stereo is now implemented, and the ledger reports 99/99 relevant source/mock checks and 6/6 stereo-rig checks. Mixed eye projection kinds and nonstandard orthographic depth are rejected, while rig factories can fall back to stubs when registration modules were not imported. Browser and device acceptance are separate.

outcomes.description: Add pivot-aware transforms through scene nodes, runtime handles and serialized projects; preserve old defaults.
outcomes.reason: Authored pivots feed transform composition, runtime handles expose validated changes and an origin default, and scene serialization retains pivots while accepting old documents.

outcomes.description: Pivot-aware atomic preserve-world reparent, transforms and hierarchy updates. Exclusive execution owner: wp02_scene. Source verification: tests/unit/scene/pivot-transform.test.ts.
outcomes.reason: Reparenting refreshes ancestor transforms and calculates the pivot-aware replacement before changing links; source fixtures cover preserved world matrices, shear and singular-parent rejection.

outcomes.description: Implement actual root-app initialization, render submission, textures, materials, shadows and presentation using the native device. Implement and test deferred, meshlet and visibility-buffer drawing paths with explicit capability fallback
outcomes.reason: Root native initialization, rendering and alternative pipeline selection are wired, with fallback. The device still explicitly rejects substantive material variants including diffuse and refractive transmission, so this broad backend row is incomplete.

outcomes.description: memory budget behavior. Unsupported features must produce precise diagnostics
outcomes.reason: Sampled textures and the native point arena have explicit budget admission and diagnostics, but these targeted limits do not establish a unified GPU memory budget across all resource types.

outcomes.description: Implement capability negotiation, queue/resource ownership, loss/recovery, full draw-state mapping, multiple vertex streams, integer formats, explicit depth convention, shader-buffer layout and color/texture contracts. Consume the WP-31 state mapper rather than silently reducing state to a blend boolean.
outcomes.reason: Native device creation, vertex streams and draw-state mapping are wired; bounded MRT and canvas paths have reported source/mock checks. Alternative depth modes and layered, depth-only or compare render targets are explicitly rejected, so the broader backend contract remains partial.

outcomes.description: Replace unconditional rejection with a functional explicit experimental opt-in once source contracts pass; promote supported/default-selection policy only after applicable rendered acceptance.
outcomes.reason: The source exposes an explicit experimental native-backend option and attempts real initialized rendering with capability checks; promotion and rendered acceptance are not implied by this source classification.

outcomes.description: explicit fallback
outcomes.reason: Backend selection has explicit allowFallback semantics, throws when fallback is disallowed, and reports the active fallback and bounded reason when allowed.

outcomes.description: WebGL2
outcomes.reason: Root renderer creation selects WebGL2, and source paths handle resize, multiple views, context loss and restore rebuilding. This is source coverage, not browser or candidate verification.

outcomes.description: Implement voxel collection, volume updates and cone-traced indirect lighting with bounded quality tiers.
outcomes.reason: Bounded quality tiers, explicit triangle voxel collection, cell updates, cone tracing and native shader sampling exist; volume construction uses documented CPU fallback.

outcomes.description: Parse admitted symmetric and two-dimensional photometric profiles with units, angular interpolation, linear lamp/multiplier factors and strict bounds.
outcomes.reason: The public loader parses bounded Type-C symmetric and two-dimensional tables, units, factors and interpolated angular samples; unsupported coordinate systems are explicitly rejected.

outcomes.description: shadow maps/filters
outcomes.reason: The renderer invokes shadow-map orchestration, and hard/PCF filter kernels are present. This narrow row does not assert support for every primitive or backend combination.

outcomes.description: Replace attributed shader code with independently authored, standards-based behavior and preserve supported material inputs.
outcomes.reason: Independently authored lobe candidates exist in an opt-in generated WebGPU preview, but the active physical lobe call chunks still carry attributed composition and some preview combinations are explicitly rejected.

outcomes.description: Ambient, hemisphere, directional, point, spot, rectangular-area, photometric and projected lights; physically meaningful units, shadow maps/filters, cascades, environment lighting, reflection probes, light-probe grids, incremental light baking and voxel-based indirect lighting where supported.
outcomes.reason: Many requested light, shadow, probe and voxel paths exist. Projected spot images now reach the public renderer on an opt-in WebGL2/PVR generated-forward path, but WebGPU, clustered, graph/custom, deformation and other projected combinations remain unsupported. The coordinated projected-light source runs reported 34/34 and 73/73; the broader lighting row remains partial.

outcomes.description: Cover lobe energy, min/max, photometry, projected texture orientation and invalid inputs.
outcomes.reason: Authored source tests cover the listed energy, parameter bounds, photometry, projected orientation and invalid-input categories. The projected orientation cases evaluate actual GLSL scalar expressions against numerical values and an independent CPU reference; the projected-helper source run reports 34/34 tests passed. This row is source test coverage for bounded paths, not GPU pixel acceptance or completion of every physical lobe variant.

outcomes.description: Test sorting, stability policy, limits and resource cleanup.
outcomes.reason: This merged source row has concrete sort/stability and cleanup assertions, cross-backend texture/sampler limit cases, portable storage-layout cases, and the graph-contact/hot-reload contract document. Source coverage is distinct from a claim that every suite passed on the current candidate.

outcomes.description: resolving
outcomes.reason: Both devices implement a single-color multisample resolve, while WebGL multisampled multiple attachments/layers and WebGPU sampleable depth resolve remain rejected. WebGPU MRT is currently single-sample only, so its new multi-attachment path does not establish multisampled MRT resolve. The parent reported a passing mock-source adjacency run including MRT; real-device acceptance is separate.

outcomes.description: Node graphs have typed values, explicit inputs/outputs, compile diagnostics, stable serialization and per-backend feature negotiation. A graph must support material color, normal, roughness, metalness, emissive, alpha and vertex position; additional render, compute and storage operations are owned by WP-05.
outcomes.reason: Typed graph IR includes the named material outputs, validation and diagnostics; the public adapter serializes graphs, compiles both shader languages, and rejects backend-incompatible storage.

outcomes.description: ownership
outcomes.reason: Supported device-created attachment textures are claimed by their creating device and foreign-device aliases are rejected; the native target paths own and retire their allocations. This is source-level ownership coverage of supported target types, not a claim that every target variant is implemented or accepted.

outcomes.description: format selection
outcomes.reason: Capability-based format selection and native compressed mapping exist; WebGPU now uploads complete decoded fallbacks for 2D and 2D-array mips with feature, size and opacity checks. Cube fallbacks and replacing a compressed fallback after edits remain unsupported. The parent reported a passing mock-source adjacency run including the array suite; strict TypeScript and GPU/browser acceptance are not inferred.

outcomes.description: Define Aura-owned graph types, construction, serialization, diagnostics, and migration from the existing node graph.
outcomes.reason: Typed graph construction, validation and serialization exist, but migration explicitly rejects unsupported prior graph nodes and alpha-test migration.

outcomes.description: Add typed history, mask, transition, pixelation, halftone, glitch, dot-screen, lens-dirt and afterimage options.
outcomes.reason: Typed mask, transition, pixelation, halftone, glitch, dot-screen, lens-dirt and afterimage builders exist; generic history controls remain internal and are not exposed by the specified public builder.

outcomes.description: Complete depth/normal/motion inputs and temporal handling; add missing effect families and composable ordering, resize and disposal.
outcomes.reason: Depth, velocity and bounded native depth of field are wired; WebGL custom passes now accept a validated borrowed reactive input, while normal inputs remain explicitly unavailable and WebGPU temporal v2 is rejected. Wider effect families and combinations remain incomplete.

outcomes.description: Replace module-global history with app/device/view/frame-owned state; advance previous transforms once per authored frame and use stable runtime object identities instead of labels.
outcomes.reason: Renderer histories are view-owned and root draw identities are stable; an additive scoped compatibility factory and explicit reset target exist. The one-argument compatibility reset and legacy slot still share a singleton, so complete removal of global history is unfinished.

outcomes.description: Source-test independently authored effects, alpha and depth behavior. Exclusive execution owner: wp06_post. Source verification: Direct Vitest for this file.
outcomes.reason: Independent scalar alpha/depth references and shader-structure tests exist alongside optical references; the specified suite largely compares separate helper math and shader strings, so comprehensive effect behavior is not established. This refresh did not execute the tests.

outcomes.description: Provide independently authored native-GPU counterparts.
outcomes.reason: Native-GPU morphological-AA shader stages exist, but no rendering-source consumer of those WGSL stages was found and the device post-pass allowlist does not include that mode.

outcomes.description: Own current/previous color and depth, reactive masks and resize/device generations; retire detached history resources.
outcomes.reason: Per-view color and depth history is allocated, retired and tracked across changes, but reactive input is explicitly caller-owned and borrowed rather than owned by the history system.

outcomes.description: Production decoder/worker URLs match development URLs under root/nested deployment bases
outcomes.reason: One normalized URL/output mapping drives decoder and worker paths for development, emitted assets, and preview; source tests include nested deployment. Browser or installed-package execution is not asserted.

outcomes.description: Resolve dependency identity and relative paths correctly; prevent cycles before awaiting; scope cache, requests and subscriber ownership.
outcomes.reason: Source resolves dependency identities and checks cycles before awaiting, partitions acquisition and subscriber ownership, and cancels independently. The updated safe-sharing scale fixture passed in a 109-test source group; this is not candidate-bound verification.

outcomes.description: Use one validated deployment base and decoder output path across development, build and static preview.
outcomes.reason: The validated deployment resolver produces a shared decoder URL and output path, used by config, development, build and static preview.

outcomes.description: Make resident data and counters agree, scope budgets per device, bound jobs and allow retries after transient failures. WP-07 and WP-25.
outcomes.reason: A device-owned residency controller, allocation accounting, retry mechanisms and bounded jobs exist. The legacy glTF texture-budget call omits a device, and retention of usable 2D mip sources is optional and incomplete, so device-scoped accounting is not established for all texture paths.

outcomes.description: Rendered option behavior is checked end to end; unsupported values return stable diagnostics instead of silent approximations.
outcomes.reason: Model option source tests exercise validation and bridge behavior, and a rendered-test fixture covers a material variant and custom shader. End-to-end coverage of all named model options is not established; test source is not a browser pass.

outcomes.description: Partition in-flight and persistent caches by effective request context; hash or otherwise protect sensitive material, and ensure one caller's abort cannot cancel another.
outcomes.reason: Main asset, glTF and audio-manager caches now use request/security identity and subscriber-aware cancellation. A SampleSlices instance can still retain fetched and decoded audio across an ambient authorization change without explicit invalidation.

outcomes.description: Import and use PVR through its admitted typed public path with documented supported variants, malformed-input limits, provenance and resource disposal.
outcomes.reason: Typed PVR v3 admission inspects bounded bytes, records digest metadata and connects direct material and caller-owned runtime paths with disposal. Unsupported encodings, metadata orientation and premultiplied pixels remain rejected. The ledger records 56/56 coordinated CLI admission source tests including PVR; installed and device acceptance remain separate.

outcomes.description: USD/USDZ geometry, materials, transforms, cameras, lights and animation where representable.
outcomes.reason: The importer translates bounded USDA and stored USDZ meshes, materials, cameras, lights and some transforms and animation. Binary crate layers, composition and some animated transform stacks remain unsupported.

outcomes.description: MD2
outcomes.reason: The opt-in version 8 adapter reports its loss diagnostics and bounds projected output and decoded typed payload. Root typed-model and installed rendering remain unestablished, and the limits do not cap PCX temporaries or total heap.

outcomes.description: photometric profiles
outcomes.reason: Type-C measured profiles feed generated forward lighting, but external tilt and Type-A/B inputs are unsupported; custom/graph shaders, unsupported draws, clustered conditions and unsupported skinning use diagnosed fallback, leaving profile breadth incomplete.

outcomes.description: return stable diagnostics for malformed or unsupported inputs.
outcomes.reason: Image, VOX and USD loaders report bounded malformed or unsupported conditions through distinct typed-code and message-prefix mechanisms; equivalent stable diagnostic coverage across all listed importers has not been established.

outcomes.description: Import and use VOX through its admitted typed public path with documented supported variants, malformed-input limits, provenance and resource disposal.
outcomes.reason: Bounded v150/200 typed admission, version-and-digest metadata, opt-in public adapter, loader/asset-bound version validation and owned disposal are implemented. The selected frame is flattened into a static mesh, live hierarchy and animation are lost, physical material properties are not rendered and unrecognized chunks are diagnosed; format breadth remains partial. The ledger reports 56/56 coordinated CLI admission and 36/36 registry/public-loader source checks; these are not installed or device acceptance.

outcomes.description: OBJ
outcomes.reason: The opt-in public OBJ writer emits scene geometry, material dependencies and structured loss warnings; a small independent source reader checks a triangle against authored fixture expectations.

outcomes.description: Implement every exporter in the WP-09 table with an independently specified capability matrix and a typed result.
outcomes.reason: The opt-in entry exposes the listed exporter modules, a typed result and warnings, and an independently declared format capability matrix; optional encoder limitations are represented.

outcomes.description: animation
outcomes.reason: The glTF writer emits animation samplers and target channels with LINEAR, STEP and CUBICSPLINE handling and validates key data; a source test exercises exported animation reloading.

outcomes.description: Export OBJ through its public path, preserving supported data with explicit structured loss and independently verified round trips.
outcomes.reason: Public OBJ export and structured warnings are present and an independent reader checks triangle positions/faces. Independent round-trip coverage for the complete supported material, texture, line, point and color scope is not established by that fixture.

outcomes.description: Export scene graph, meshes, materials, cameras, lights, skins, morphs, animation and dependencies with explicit loss warnings.
outcomes.reason: The glTF writer constructs scene nodes, geometry, materials, cameras, lights, skins, morph-capable meshes, animation and dependencies and collects structured warnings for unsupported data.

outcomes.description: including diffuse roughness
outcomes.reason: The typed material contract and glTF writer support the diffuse-roughness factor and texture, with texture handling through the exporter.

outcomes.description: Add scalar-volume slices and rendering with clipping, transfer functions and lifecycle tests.
outcomes.reason: Standalone and typed root-scene WebGL2 paths implement slices, transfer functions, local clipping and lifecycle source tests. WebGPU, scene-wide clipping and several output or view combinations remain explicitly unsupported.

outcomes.description: spherical harmonics
outcomes.reason: The loader validates and preserves supported spherical-harmonic coefficients, and the splat renderer evaluates degrees through four against the transformed camera direction.

outcomes.description: define what happens on unsupported backends.
outcomes.reason: Unsupported volume devices, splat depth modes and missing compositing adapters have explicit errors rather than silent fallback.

outcomes.description: Render scalar volume textures/slices with transfer functions and clipping.
outcomes.reason: A typed root-scene scalar-volume node now reaches the renderer with slices, transfer stops and local clip planes, in addition to the standalone volume pass. The implementation remains WebGL2-only and rejects global clipping, postprocessing, multiview and other renderer combinations, so the full source scope is not complete.

outcomes.description: Test camera movement, depth, transparency, visible color, clipping, resize and disposal.
outcomes.reason: The authored browser specification covers the named scenarios on bounded standalone paths, but scene-clipped splats are explicitly rejected and scalar-volume root combinations remain restricted. This classification is about authored source and unsupported variants; it does not assert browser acceptance was run.

outcomes.description: PLY/SPLAT/KSPLAT/SPZ
outcomes.reason: PLY, SPLAT and versioned SPZ parsing are implemented, but KSPLAT decoding depends on a caller-provided codec rather than a native wire decoder.

outcomes.description: shape-preserving key optimization
outcomes.reason: The optimizer conservatively preserves curved and tangent-bearing tracks and drops repeated constant interior keys from other tracks. Candidate-wide verification is separate.

outcomes.description: repeat
outcomes.reason: Repeat mode computes finite/infinite crossings and finish signals; its reverse-boundary regression has concrete assertions. The ledger reports 42 focused and adjacent source tests passed with scoped TypeScript, not candidate-wide or browser acceptance.

outcomes.description: boolean
outcomes.reason: Boolean tracks are typed, sampled as discrete values, exported, and passed through mixer blending.

outcomes.description: material-property tracks
outcomes.reason: Material animation reaches live renderer uniforms, including guarded normal-scale and occlusion-strength bindings, but only a bounded set of material leaves is mapped; unsupported leaves and invalid live bindings are reported rather than silently treated as applied.

outcomes.description: add generic source adapters.
outcomes.reason: Media-element, stream, and external-node adapters are exported, with borrowed/owned teardown and explicit non-buffer transport limits.

outcomes.description: Preserve clip, track and mixer coverage using independent expected results.
outcomes.reason: The source test suites contain local clip, track and mixer assertions and independently calculated reference expectations. This states what the tests implement, not that their current candidate-bound execution passed.

outcomes.description: procedural poses
outcomes.reason: Source exposes procedural look-at and iterative CCD constraints which calculate and write skeleton pose rotations through the animation lanes subpath.

outcomes.description: Test actual browser-shaped objects, reference-space loss and session transitions.
outcomes.reason: Browser-shaped mocks exercise session acquisition, null tracking, asynchronous session transitions and reference-space reset. A distinct reference-space-loss scenario remains unlocated; these test names and source assertions do not establish a current passing run.

outcomes.description: Consume native viewer, hand and hit-test APIs; expose input-source/select/squeeze, reference-space reset, visibility and cancellation lifecycles.
outcomes.reason: The source samples viewer, hand and hit-test data, routes input-source/select/squeeze, reference-space reset and visibility events, and removes listeners and cancels owned work on session teardown.

outcomes.description: Sample native XR viewer poses, hand joints and hit-test results with their reference spaces
outcomes.reason: The controller acquires the selected and hit-test viewer spaces, samples viewer poses, iterable hand joints and hit results in the selected reference space, and cancels owned hit-test sources during teardown.

outcomes.description: Preserve listener lifecycle expectations for native interaction. Exclusive execution owner: wp12_controls. Source verification: Direct Vitest for this file.
outcomes.reason: The recently updated source test now enumerates all ten native input listener types, checks one registration each and checks disposal; InputSystem registers the same types and removes them on disposal. No source-test execution is claimed for this revision.

outcomes.description: Immersive
outcomes.reason: The public app runtime requests immersive sessions and renders their per-eye views. Its source presentation route requires a WebGL2 context and rejects unavailable render paths; this classification does not assert WebGPU presentation or physical-device acceptance.

outcomes.description: Attribute formats
outcomes.reason: Typed and normalized attributes with separate streams are modeled, and the WebGPU mapper now includes scalar 8- and 16-bit integer and normalized formats. Three-component packed integers, several unnormalized integer-to-float mappings and instance divisors other than one still reject, so the format breadth remains incomplete.

outcomes.description: shared buffers
outcomes.reason: Geometry retains shared vertex, additional-stream and index buffers, releasing them after the final geometry owner; its managed writable path copies shared data. Direct buffer disposal invalidates all users and direct raw edits stay shared. The cited source tests use a mock device; no new run is asserted.

outcomes.description: UV unwrapping
outcomes.reason: The public atlas supports planar charts and an opt-in seed-normal projection for gently curved faces, with bounded distortion, overlap checks and attribute remapping. The angle and plane limits still force seams for broader curvature, so general curved unwrapping remains incomplete. Regression source exists; the corrected test revision is not claimed as passed.

outcomes.description: Verify topology and counts against independently authored expectations.
outcomes.reason: The requested regression source specifies analytical coordinates, winding, topology and shape areas independently, including concave contours and holes. This classification concerns the authored test source; its execution is not asserted.

outcomes.description: shapes
outcomes.reason: Exported planar shape generation resolves contours and holes and uses the independent triangulation entry. The shape implementation itself explicitly says its current rewrite remains under provenance and compatibility review; independent-source completion is therefore unresolved. This does not assert that the active triangulator was copied.

outcomes.description: Provide a parametric patch-based reference geometry with controllable tessellation.
outcomes.reason: The source defines an authored bicubic patch reference shape with selectable components and an integer tessellation count from one to 64, and exports the builder. Its focused source tests are present; no execution is claimed here.

outcomes.description: Test transforms, hot updates, empty geometry and disposal.
outcomes.reason: Authored unit cases cover transformed endpoints, resampling/hot updates, empty geometry, runtime mounting and disposal; no current-candidate source execution is asserted.

outcomes.description: Test assistive labels, pointer routing, screenshot output, resize and cleanup.
outcomes.reason: Authored browser spec covers accessible labels, pointer routing, resize, restoration and screenshot output with source assertions. This is source coverage only: browser acceptance has not run.

outcomes.description: Spatial DOM labels
outcomes.reason: Spatial labels have a public addon subpath and an actual renderer with projection, visibility, stacking, interaction and disposal.

outcomes.description: resources
outcomes.reason: Dynamic helpers resample geometry, apply transforms and visibility, and replace or remove owned runtime nodes; current registry code invokes compiled subtree removal or a scene update.

outcomes.description: Add animation path, audio orientation, probe/grid, octree, collider, area light, texture, vertex-normal and tangent helpers.
outcomes.reason: All listed helper builders are implemented for path, audio, probe/grid, octree, collider, area light, texture, vertex normals and tangents and exposed through engine helper nodes.

outcomes.description: Provide 2D and perspective DOM labels with transforms, stacking, accessibility and documented occlusion.
outcomes.reason: Addon public subpath implements screen/perspective transforms, depth stacking, ARIA, pointer behavior, documented anchor-only occlusion and lifecycle restoration.

outcomes.description: Add grounded sky, shadow projection and volume slice objects using existing renderer facilities.
outcomes.reason: The three objects are public and now have GLSL and bounded WGSL routes, including gradient sky and mutable volume slices; object-inclusive mock/source checks are reported. Shadow projection is explicitly a caster-bounds approximation, not a geometry silhouette, and native sky rejects other sky variants, so broader projection/sky behavior remains partial.

outcomes.description: Test determinism, bounds, topology, budgets, undo data and teardown.
outcomes.reason: Source tests cover deterministic output, bounds, topology, budgets, undo and teardown across the generator and editing tools. The ledger reports an object-inclusive source run, separately from browser acceptance.

outcomes.description: tube painting
outcomes.reason: An exported tube painter builds editable geometry from a point path and supplies bounded teardown behavior.

outcomes.description: Add deterministic convex fracture geometry and explicit unsupported cases.
outcomes.reason: The public addon implements bounded seeded or plane-driven convex fracture, validates closed convex topology and rejects unsupported inputs; source tests exercise determinism, geometry and limits.

outcomes.description: Reuse the existing terrain, sky, water and scatter facilities where they satisfy the contract; do not replace working paths.
outcomes.reason: Current source reuses scatter, supplies terrain-compatible data and uses the existing sky builder; this spot check cannot establish the historical no-replacement condition for every pre-existing facility, including water.

outcomes.description: Add path-based tube drawing with normals, caps and disposal.
outcomes.reason: The public tube painter generates path geometry with transported normals and optional caps, supports editing and limits, and has idempotent disposal.

outcomes.description: Transfer canvas ownership once
outcomes.reason: The host tracks transferred canvases, IDs increase monotonically, resize/input use snapshots, and errors/cancellation are routed through the worker protocol.

outcomes.description: Verify rendered pixels, resize, input and clean teardown on supported backends.
outcomes.reason: Browser test source covers pixels, input, resize and disposal on WebGL2; its WebGPU branch disables the input bridge and omits the same input scenario. No browser acceptance result is implied.

outcomes.description: Test message ordering, transfer ownership, errors, cancellation and disposal.
outcomes.reason: The worker source enforces request IDs and cancellation, and focused test bodies exercise ordered traffic, transferable ownership, failure and disposal. A ledger checkpoint reports a prior 42-test worker source run; this refresh did not execute tests.

outcomes.description: Add explicit OffscreenCanvas handling without breaking DOM targets.
outcomes.reason: Canvas resolution handles OffscreenCanvas and DOM canvases/containers, and the public worker entry uses the offscreen worker route.

outcomes.description: resource transfer
outcomes.reason: The worker API transfers scene-owned buffers and other transferable resources with ownership checks; realm-local live texture handles are explicitly rejected.

outcomes.description: teardown
outcomes.reason: Worker, renderer and event-bridge teardown handle pending requests, bounded shutdown and idempotent pointer-capture release. The ledger reports 42 focused/adjacent source tests and scoped strict typing for the pointer-capture revision; this refresh did not rerun them.

outcomes.description: Connect graph editing to real material state and the renderer compiler
outcomes.reason: Typed graph editing, undo and device compilation are connected for supported meshes, but the live editor explicitly rejects imported skinned or morph-target meshes. Reclassified from implemented to reflect an existing unsupported variant, not a regression.

outcomes.description: Test graph validation, undo, persistence, resource selection and errors.
outcomes.reason: The editor test source includes actual graph validation, undo, persistence, selection and error assertions. Existence of these assertions is not a claim that this candidate has passed the suite.

outcomes.description: Expose actual frame passes, draw/resource counts, timings and diagnostics.
outcomes.reason: Live counts and some measured CPU pass data reach the editor, but several phases are explicitly unobserved and aggregate/per-pass GPU timing is null. A separate partial GPU-view timing field does not close the editor inspector gap.

outcomes.description: Scene/project editor
outcomes.reason: A project/scene editor shell is present with hierarchy, inspector, material, texture, timeline and profiler panels, serialization, and a real project runtime.

outcomes.description: avoid fixture-only visualizations.
outcomes.reason: The editor reads real texture and frame sources; full frame tracing is explicitly incomplete. Renderer GPU-view timing is a separate, explicitly partial field, while the editor inspector still reads nullable aggregate/per-pass GPU timing.

outcomes.description: do not introduce remote font services.
outcomes.reason: The editor styles load locally served licensed font cuts and provide local fallbacks; source checks cover packaged font assets. This observation is scoped to the editor app.

outcomes.description: complete every row and retain proof of public exposure, not merely internal classes.
outcomes.reason: The ledger contains 1,901 outcomes, but only three have public-entrypoint mappings, none has source-evidence entries, and none records source completion as complete. The requested full public-exposure tracking is incomplete.

outcomes.description: Keep supported API examples and claim boundaries current. Exclusive execution owner: wp18_recovery. Source verification: Documentation link and snippet checks.
outcomes.reason: Guides and claim boundaries exist, but the quickstart says toon is only a screen effect while the root source exports a material namespace with material.toon. The targeted documentation is therefore not fully current; no snippet test was run.

outcomes.description: device
outcomes.reason: The evidence validator distinguishes physical devices from software or injected runs. The inspected automated browser runner records unverified or software device classes, and a complete physical-device source runner across device classes was not established; this is a tooling coverage limit, not a claim about a missing live receipt.

outcomes.description: Provide one isolated, runnable scenario per capability family with no unrelated engine runtime.
outcomes.reason: Ten separately mounted typed-model scenarios and a project harness are present, but their catalog does not cover every roadmap capability family, including spatial audio and XR.

outcomes.description: Synchronize source API appendix with generated public documentation and bounded claims. Exclusive execution owner: wp18_docs/public_api_docs. Source verification: API documentation contract tests.
outcomes.reason: The appendix is embedded verbatim and carries bounded claims, but the generated document header differs from both current generator variants, so whole-document validation cannot match. The API-docs source test also compares against a render that omits the appendix. No test was run.

outcomes.description: Provide runnable Aura3D-owned examples for each delivered capability family using typed admitted assets.
outcomes.reason: Aura3D-owned recipes describe ten typed-model scenarios and a separate advanced-lighting recipe with scoped claims. They do not provide an example for every delivered capability family; no example was executed during this audit.

outcomes.description: Integrate runtime target, worker, backend and diagnostics contracts.
outcomes.reason: Readiness, backend and diagnostics types coexist with a worker path that accepts OffscreenCanvas. The main AuraAppTarget excludes OffscreenCanvas, and the worker source identifies a DOM-only scene-compiler type seam, so full target/worker contract integration remains incomplete.

outcomes.description: repeated like-for-like workloads report startup
outcomes.reason: The source fixes workloads and records startup metrics across three separately launched browser sessions, with identity and workload validation in the analyzer. This measures implementation of the instrumentation only; no actual candidate measurements or browser acceptance are asserted.

outcomes.description: Support verified Git-free staging manifests, recompute every required input and bind unchanged tested snapshots to the freeze commit; separate reviewed administrative records from implementation identity.
outcomes.reason: The source verifies Git-free staged entries and bytes, rejects undeclared inputs, separates administrative records from implementation identity, and binds matching source fingerprints, lockfile and archive hashes to a committed freeze. No current candidate or release completion is asserted.

outcomes.description: ESM/CommonJS installed consumers
outcomes.reason: An installed-consumer source suite covers ESM entrypoints and the CommonJS math bridge, but the engine root and most subpaths lack dedicated CommonJS export conditions. Broader installed CommonJS and supported-runtime behavior is not established; the suite was not run in this audit.

outcomes.description: Test historical and new inventories, missing/duplicate packages and identity/rollback requirements.
outcomes.reason: The requested test source covers historical/current inventory membership, missing and duplicate entries, source identity and changed artifact bytes. No rollback-specific assertion was found in this file, so the described test coverage remains incomplete.

outcomes.description: Validate the global gate before analyzing --input candidate-bound remote measurements for fixed Aura3D workloads; reject missing samples/identity and report startup/frame/draw/memory/bundle results. Source tests may exercise pure analysis with synthetic fixtures but must not launch a browser or claim acceptance.
outcomes.reason: The analysis source invokes the supplied global-gate validator before loading candidate data, verifies archive/workload/session identity, and compares startup, frame, draw, memory and bundle metrics. Synthetic source tests exist; no browser measurement or acceptance run is claimed.

outcomes.description: Repeatedly mount, load, resize, lose/recover where supported, unload and dispose without growing live resource counts.
outcomes.reason: Authored browser spec implements four mount/load/resize/unload/dispose cycles, context-loss recovery and zero live buffer/texture/program assertions. This is source coverage only: browser acceptance has not run.

outcomes.description: Run source checks, package tests and source-phase installed consumers before freeze; run remote browser behavior and visual tests afterward. Keep actual test names, versions, run IDs, candidate hashes, backend, device and limitations with results.
outcomes.reason: The runner defines source checks, package tests and source-phase consumer reports before gated browser work; a complete candidate-bound source execution and frozen gate are not yet established.

outcomes.description: avoid uploading unrelated repository assets.
outcomes.reason: Native acceptance stages the complete gate-listed candidate inputs, while source identity broadly admits repository files and assets; no per-job exclusion of unrelated assets is evident, and legacy staging copies whole fixture directories.

outcomes.description: Test partial/unowned outcomes, equal-count but different ID sets, missing/skipped source checks, tampered files, stale commits/artifacts, early browser invocation and valid code-complete-to-acceptance handoff without launching a browser/provider job.
outcomes.reason: The expanded synthetic test source includes a positive emit/revalidation handoff plus skipped, tampered and missing source results and pre-provider rejection. Explicit cases for partial or unowned outcomes, equal-count differing outcome IDs and stale freeze commits were not located, so the specified test matrix remains partial.

outcomes.description: Implement and source-test the single global phase gate. Require its matching code-complete record at acceptance entrypoints before job submission and inside the remote task; the source runner must reject any browser/acceptance argv before starting a process.
outcomes.reason: Native routes validate the gate before submission and in-task, source argv is guarded, and a synthetic source-handoff test exists; browser legacy selectors remain outside the native gate and some required negative handoff cases remain absent from test source.

outcomes.description: Add a source-only serverless runner, complete suites, generated-map ownership, phase-specific consumer reports and a verified current API baseline. WP-19/WP-20/WP-24/WP-25.
outcomes.reason: Source runner code defines suite inventory, resolution checks, phase reports and verification of baseline archive integrity; an actual complete current-candidate source run and verified baseline report remain unestablished.

outcomes.description: Fix pooled target double release; track live leases/idle membership so simultaneous users never share one lease and counters remain nonnegative. Test foreign targets, trim, restore and outstanding handles.
outcomes.reason: The pool tracks exclusive token and legacy leases, idle ownership and generations; legacy returns are retired, foreign or duplicate releases are ignored, and restore retires outstanding targets. Tests cover concurrency, foreign releases, trim and restore; the parent reports a 91/91 pool/lease source rerun. Combined candidate typing is pending.

outcomes.description: Add success-aware readiness, app-owned context, bounded errors, event cleanup, loss/restore and deterministic lifecycle races.
outcomes.reason: Readiness, event cleanup and bounded restore errors have source handling and focused checks. WebGL has app remount hooks, while WebGPU recovery returns a new device and supplies no equivalent automatic restored callback, so full lifecycle recovery remains partial.

outcomes.description: Prevent acquisition after disposal, dispose late successful compiles, settle cancelled handles and retry only within the correct device generation.
outcomes.reason: Program cache rejects acquisition after disposal, settles cancelled handles, disposes late programs and invalidates results across device generations.

outcomes.description: duplicate release
outcomes.reason: Legacy target-only acquisitions are retired on release; reusable token acquisitions have distinct release identities, so stale or duplicate release cannot free a later borrower. The parent reports 91/91 focused pool/lease source checks after the legacy change; combined candidate typing remains pending.

outcomes.description: Enforce exclusive leases, idempotent release, device generations and accurate ownership. WP-21.
outcomes.reason: Token identity, retirement of target-only acquisitions, generation invalidation and explicit idle/live maps enforce the requested ownership contract. The parent reports 91/91 focused pool/lease source checks after the legacy change; no browser/device acceptance is inferred.

outcomes.description: events
outcomes.reason: Asset events use per-app captured scopes, subscriptions and disposal; the standalone compatibility channel does not share app handlers.

outcomes.description: physical-device evidence remain separate
outcomes.reason: Physical-device evidence requires an explicit distinct class and provenance and is kept separate from software, automation and injected results. Actual device evidence is a later acceptance task.

outcomes.description: Reject missing browser versions, false hardware labels and unqualified skipped cases.
outcomes.reason: The source validator rejects missing/placeholder browser versions, contradictory hardware labels and skipped scenarios without a specific reason.

outcomes.description: Supported browser, OS, device, backend and feature combinations have versioned support labels. Software, experimental, emulated and physical-device evidence remain separate.
outcomes.reason: A versioned target matrix and supported/experimental/unsupported/unverified labels exist, with evidence tiers separated. Current candidate combinations are honestly unverified; no acceptance is implied.

outcomes.description: emulated
outcomes.reason: The matrix and evidence validator explicitly classify emulated devices separately and reject labeling them physical.

outcomes.description: Build a versioned support matrix with default-flags desktop projects and separately labeled experimental, software and physical-device results. WP-22.
outcomes.reason: A versioned matrix defines default-launch desktop automation and separately labeled software, experimental and physical-device targets; target results remain unverified until acceptance.

outcomes.description: Route browser-project forwarding and result/artifact transport through WP-20
outcomes.reason: The configured project selection is forwarded into the remote runner, which stages reports and fails on missing artifact-transfer status. The source was inspected only; no remote job was started.

outcomes.description: Exercise both declared supported peer major versions, StrictMode double mounts, Suspense, error boundaries, prop updates, input and scene disposal using packed packages.
outcomes.reason: The browser acceptance harness source restores separate packed consumers for both peer majors and contains assertions for hydration, StrictMode, Suspense, errors, input, updates and cleanup. Implemented means the harness source exists; browser acceptance has not been run and its behavior is not claimed as passed.

outcomes.description: deliver cancellation/failure through a stable boundary and do not update unmounted components.
outcomes.reason: The adapter aborts and revision-guards renderer readiness, delivers errors through onError or render, and suppresses late callbacks after cleanup. This is source inspection, not a claim of packed/browser acceptance.

outcomes.description: Scope asset resources by effective loader, request/security context and digest
outcomes.reason: Resources are bounded and keyed by loader identity, immutable descriptors/digests and security-context identity, but callers must change that identity when mutable credentials or policy change; policy mutation is not automatically detected.

outcomes.description: The existing React integration handles both documented peer majors
outcomes.reason: Readiness, SSR, Suspense and disposal paths exist, but cache isolation depends on callers changing the security-context identity when policy changes. Peer-matrix browser execution remains deferred and is not counted as accepted.

outcomes.description: Test server-safe imports, resource identity, retries, cancellation and late completions.
outcomes.reason: The source suite contains assertions for server-safe import, descriptor/context identity, cancellation, retry and late completion. The ledger reports an earlier mock/source React run; neither current-candidate coverage nor browser acceptance is inferred.

outcomes.description: StrictMode
outcomes.reason: Mount cleanup aborts readiness and disposes the app; owned preload cleanup allows StrictMode effect replay. Mock source tests contain explicit assertions; this does not claim a packed browser run.

outcomes.description: Verify native isolated consumers, package conditions, optional peers and SSR-safe imports.
outcomes.reason: The root-candidate smoke harness includes SSR, browser conditions and absent/present optional-peer cases. Standalone physics still declares the backend adapter as a required dependency and eagerly imports it in PhysicsWorld; a complete backend-free standalone consumer contract is not established.

outcomes.description: Include or explicitly install promised environment assets in generated templates.
outcomes.reason: The scaffold copies and validates the five packaged probe sets and its existing HDRIs. The public look catalog also references numerous HDRI files absent from the four shipped HDR files, so all selectable promised environment assets are not yet supplied.

outcomes.description: Validate the complete supported example catalog rather than a small selected subset.
outcomes.reason: The catalog is discovered from public and release-classified source references, augmented with enumerated capability scenarios, and checked for missing, duplicate, skipped or failed install/build results; this does not assert a passing run.

outcomes.description: Verify peer, package-manager, module-condition and isolation reporting.
outcomes.reason: The source suite and matrix validator cover package managers, React/optional-peer combinations, module conditions, isolation identities and rejected missing or fabricated reports. No fresh execution is claimed.

outcomes.description: Build every promised template and capability-family example from an isolated, untouched scaffold. The harness may substitute the candidate package only; it must report and fail on missing dependencies or skipped required checks.
outcomes.reason: The harness stages isolated projects from a candidate and enumerates examples, but the ten capability examples do not cover the breadth of promised families; complete untouched-scaffold coverage remains unfinished.

outcomes.description: Typecheck every applicable documented snippet against packed packages and report explicit exemptions.
outcomes.reason: The source harness discovers public fenced documentation, stages packed candidate declarations, compiles applicable snippets, and records exemptions and diagnostics. This audit does not claim that the current candidate passed.

outcomes.description: Establish independently reproducible workloads for one primitive, product scene, dense instances, animation, a game loop, effects and asset import. Fix scene/asset hashes, seed, active look, quality, viewport, device pixel ratio, browser and backend.
outcomes.reason: The seven source workloads fix the seed, look, quality, viewport, DPR, backend and referenced asset digests; workload and instrumentation sources are hashed. The selected browser and version are recorded, and like-for-like comparison requires matching browser and device identity. This does not claim the workloads have been executed.

outcomes.description: retain p50/p95/p99 frame and CPU durations, startup/first drawable frame, requests, raw/gzip/Brotli bytes, allocations and live resource counts. If timing or hardware is unavailable, report no-data.
outcomes.reason: The workload source collects first reported drawable startup, frame and synchronous submission percentiles, requests, compressed and raw response-body bytes, and observed resource allocation/lifetime; unavailable metrics are recorded with reasons. The probe schedules three independent sessions of 300 frames. This classifies source instrumentation only; no current measurements or browser execution are asserted.

outcomes.description: Accept --source-report; validate current candidate/tarball/project hashes and measure root/addon/React slices from untouched source-phase consumers without requiring browser receipts.
outcomes.reason: The source accepts a source report and validated candidate plan, restores or copies verified consumer projects, rechecks source and installed-package hashes, and bundles root, game-addon and React slices without browser receipts. This does not assert a current installed-candidate measurement.

outcomes.description: Reproduce and meet the repository's existing gzip budgets: 190,000 bytes for the core critical path, 250,000 for the product starter, 400,000 for the cinematic starter and 480,000 for the mini-game starter. The checked-in overages are historical measurements
outcomes.reason: The original four budget thresholds and measurement checker are present. The checked-in report explicitly describes its overruns as historical and not a current candidate result; source evidence does not establish that the budgets are met.

outcomes.description: Use real asynchronous device timers where available; label CPU time and unsupported/disjoint GPU results correctly.
outcomes.reason: A selected WebGPU forward draw can now be timed asynchronously through an opt-in source path; CPU and unsupported/lost states remain distinct. Normal WebGPU frame telemetry is still unconnected, and a single pass is not a frame duration.

outcomes.description: Existing bundle budgets pass without being raised; repeated like-for-like workloads report startup, p50/p95/p99, bytes, resource counts and available hardware timing. Counters and software results are not visual or hardware proof.
outcomes.reason: Unraised budget definitions and repeatable workload measurement code exist, but the available report is historical and does not establish current budget compliance or candidate-bound workload results. Measurement instrumentation is not itself a passing budget.

outcomes.description: Compile font assets, shaping results and atlas updates to visible text.
outcomes.reason: Font-backed shaping feeds SDF image and mesh/texture compilation, and live edits rebuild and swap resources. The atlas is temporary CPU data rather than a retained GPU atlas receiving incremental glyph updates.

outcomes.description: Load admitted licensed font data and metadata with bounded decoding.
outcomes.reason: The loader requires license metadata and bounds encoded bytes, declared expanded size and font tables, but delegates decoding to FontFace without an enforced runtime limit on the decoder allocation; the entire bounded-decoding contract is not established.

outcomes.description: Request existing geometry and public type changes from their WP-01/WP-19 owners; verify source, pixel output, interaction and resource teardown.
outcomes.reason: Source and browser test code covers shaped text, line pixels, updates, and disposal; the inspected targeted suites do not exercise pointer or picking interaction for these objects. This assesses test source, not execution.

outcomes.description: Manage bounded glyph allocation, eviction, updates and GPU disposal.
outcomes.reason: The bounded atlas class implements retention, eviction, dirty uploads and optional backing disposal; world text creates a temporary CPU-only atlas and discards it, so retained GPU glyph-atlas integration is not in that public rendering path.

outcomes.description: direction
outcomes.reason: The public font-backed path supports explicit ltr/rtl and auto direction, but auto chooses RTL from a short script list rather than a complete first-strong Unicode bidi classification.

outcomes.description: Implement width, dash, gradient, clipping and alpha behavior.
outcomes.reason: Width, dashes, vertex gradients, alpha, and a clipping variant are implemented in source; clipping explicitly excludes geometry-matrix and instanced variants, with specialized depth cases retaining separate limitations.

outcomes.description: Complete or explicitly reject root behaviors, prove collider/joint/vehicle/game lifecycle and retain optional backend boundaries. WP-27.
outcomes.reason: The root game slot now produces an explicit migration error and physics/game provider isolation is staged, but the physics package still declares its backend as a required dependency and candidate installed-backend-absent behavior is unresolved.

outcomes.description: Complete supported ready/input/HUD/audio/effects/reset and disposal behavior on the full game entrypoint.
outcomes.reason: The full game mounts its supported input, HUD, audio and effects, owns reset and disposal, and now detects renderer failures while awaiting a presented draw. The ledger records 98/98 focused readiness/termination source and mock checks; unsupported effects remain explicitly rejected.

outcomes.description: Synchronize scene transforms, parent transforms and physics ownership safely.
outcomes.reason: Standalone bridging and root ownership exist, and newer source publishes supported rigid-body world poses into parent-local runtime transforms. Parented look-at, shear, reflected/singular poses and changed collider scales are rejected; broader collider/parent synchronization remains in progress and is not claimed complete.

outcomes.description: Complete deterministic stepping, contacts, sensors, continuous collision and lifecycle behavior.
outcomes.reason: The production world implements stepping, contact and sensor transitions, bounded continuous collision and disposal; this status concerns that supported source path, not experimental solver parity or acceptance.

outcomes.description: Validate installed games with manual keyboard and touch, HUD, audio/effects, pause/reset, replay and cleanup. Promote only features backed by the applicable root or subpath evidence.
outcomes.reason: The row asks for installed manual/device validation rather than a source implementation outcome; no such acceptance was run or inferred by this audit.

outcomes.description: deterministic stepping and continuous collision.
outcomes.reason: The current production physics world provides repeatable fixed-delta stepping and native continuous collision with an optional bounded adaptive-substep mode; the separate experimental native solver is not claimed complete.

outcomes.description: Conformance fixtures have documented provenance
outcomes.reason: All 21 entries in the scoped conformance manifest carry authorship, license, provenance and a digest, and test source validates those fields. The manifest separately lists 36 unverified format categories; no candidate-wide provenance claim follows.

outcomes.description: Verify actual returned/resident mip bytes, device isolation, duplicate labels and release.
outcomes.reason: Source assertions cover returned mip bytes, device isolation, duplicate labels and release with CPU data and mock devices. An authored test for the full real-device residency combination was not found.

outcomes.description: independent expected output. Claimed variants are decoded
outcomes.reason: The manifest and source/browser test implementations define independent expected results for an initial fixture subset. Numerous additional format or variant combinations are outside that authored fixture and rendering-test inventory; this is a source-coverage limitation, not a live acceptance result.

outcomes.description: Verify the texture budget against returned CPU bytes and live device residency, including same-name textures on separate devices, eviction and release.
outcomes.reason: Test source checks returned CPU bytes, duplicate labels, eviction, per-device ownership and release. The inspected residency paths use mock contexts or recorders; an authored live-device test for the full requested combination was not found.

outcomes.description: Cover nested external dependencies, invalid required/optional extensions, corrupt/truncated files, archive expansion, strict/fallback texture failures, byte integrity and independently verified export round trips.
outcomes.reason: Authored source assertions cover nested dependencies, required/optional extension behavior, truncated inputs, archive limits, strict/fallback texture errors, integrity and independently read OBJ/STL exports. A ledger checkpoint reports a historical 22/22 source run, not verification of the current candidate.

outcomes.description: Publish supported combinations, fixture method, known losses and exact evidence.
outcomes.reason: The conformance page publishes fixture method, a narrow set of supported combinations and losses, but the broader format inventory remains outside the independently verified fixture/evidence set.

outcomes.description: Exercise direct/transitive/alias/optional/peer dependencies, embedded data, review candidates and false positives.
outcomes.reason: This ID merges many source-audit, independent-math, shader-contract and replacement tasks. Independent triangulation, bounded hull and mutable math candidates exist and the hull has an opt-in public entry, but the stable math barrel still uses its existing entries and broad replacement/public compatibility is not complete.

outcomes.description: Replace reference-dependent fixtures with independently derived UV expectations.
outcomes.reason: The test source derives UV expectations from coordinate operations and fixed analytic examples, with assertions against the local implementation. Source existence does not assert a current test pass.

outcomes.description: Inspect permitted runtime network events for external engine implementation fetches.
outcomes.reason: The network-classifier source inspects supplied allowed and unexpected observations and labels engine references for review. Its documented scope does not prove event capture completeness or an executed runtime test.

outcomes.description: Treat textual references, standardized equations and fingerprint hits as review candidates, not automatic proof of copied implementation. A scanner alone cannot prove independent authorship.
outcomes.reason: Source and network audit tools explicitly treat textual/fingerprint matches as review candidates and state that neither a match nor its absence proves authorship.

outcomes.description: Verify a clean packed consumer runs offline without fetching an external engine implementation.
outcomes.reason: The harness source restores a packed consumer, blocks network access, checks a negative control and observes requests. Implemented denotes harness source coverage only; offline browser acceptance has not been run and no actual offline pass is claimed.

outcomes.description: Test direct, transitive, aliased, peer and optional dependency detection. Exclusive execution owner: wp29_provenance/dependency_graph. Source verification: Direct Vitest for this file.
outcomes.reason: The dedicated test source contains assertions for direct, transitive, aliased, peer, optional and packed dependency cases, including false positives. Presence of test code is not a claim of an executed pass.

outcomes.description: Extract and test planes for supported clip/depth ranges and optional unbounded far distance.
outcomes.reason: The targeted frustum source extracts planes for both supported clip ranges, reversed depth and unbounded far, with corresponding source test cases. No test execution is asserted by this audit.

outcomes.description: Keep projection, inverse projection and culling metadata coherent after updates.
outcomes.reason: The targeted scene Camera computes and publishes projection, inverse, view projection, frustum and metadata together; setter failure restores the previous setting. This classification is for the specified Camera.ts outcome.

outcomes.description: 3×3/4×4 matrices
outcomes.reason: The public math root exposes 3x3 and 4x4 matrices with arithmetic, inversion and transforms. The separate independently authored mutable candidate is not treated as a public replacement.

outcomes.description: depth of field
outcomes.reason: Public and WebGL depth-of-field paths exist, alongside a source/mock-tested bounded native-WebGPU route. The latter restricts scene contributors, multi-view and materials, including requiring opaque unlit triangles, so wider supported combinations remain incomplete.

outcomes.description: tiled/asymmetric views
outcomes.reason: Public perspective and moving camera builders now forward lens and tile fields, with focused source tests. Lower-level scene cameras can resize to the tile aspect before cropping instead of retaining the full-image aspect, so tiled rendering is not yet complete.

outcomes.description: line segments
outcomes.reason: The root public API exports line-segment builders and the live compiler turns independent segment pairs into corresponding geometry.

outcomes.description: sorted fallback
outcomes.reason: The standalone weighted helper owns per-view resources, accepts opaque depth and invokes sorted fallback for incompatible or unavailable paths. Renderer source uses its ordinary sorted transparent pass and does not wire the helper into weighted-mode selection, so integrated weighted rendering and fallback remain incomplete.

outcomes.description: Test every supported state, variant key, integer/normalized layout, separate instance stream and invalid combination.
outcomes.reason: The named test source covers many state mappings, pipeline keys, separate streams, selected integer/normalized layouts and invalid inputs. Its layout table samples the supported combinations rather than explicitly asserting all of them, for example unorm8x2; exhaustive requested coverage remains incomplete. Test execution is not asserted.

outcomes.description: a change in shader-affecting state must select the correct variant, while ordinary uniform edits must not cause needless recompilation.
outcomes.reason: Feature keys and warmup cover selected clipping and output variants, and source regressions cover a live map change, uniform-only reuse and actual masked shadow-program warmup. The public renderer explicitly rejects nonstandard depth conventions, so the broader clipping/depth/output integration remains incomplete. The absence of an unused generated depth warmup is not treated as a defect.

outcomes.description: Pixel-check culling, custom blend, stencil, color masks, polygon offset, depth comparison and instance data on each backend.
outcomes.reason: The browser test source specifies pixel cases for both backends and the named state and instance categories, but it skips a backend when reported unsupported; thus the source does not require successful checks on each backend. No browser acceptance execution is claimed.

outcomes.description: Define full named/custom blend, depth and alpha semantics consumed by both devices.
outcomes.reason: The shared contract defines and validates named/custom color and alpha blend components and depth comparisons. WebGL2 and native WebGPU resolve those shared semantics in their draw-state paths; hardware-specific unsupported combinations are not claimed as rendered.

outcomes.description: Map full draw state to native pipeline/dynamic state and a deterministic cache key including attachment/layout requirements.
outcomes.reason: The native path resolves fixed and dynamic state, attachment formats and vertex layouts into a deterministic pipeline key and uses it in device submission. Non-unit instance divisors, three-component packed integers and unnormalized integer-to-float layouts are still explicitly unsupported, leaving full requested layout breadth incomplete.

outcomes.description: Verify known color vectors, HDR values above one and below zero, output readback, layered/mip update isolation, changing media frames, compressed-block validation and final cleanup on supported backends.
outcomes.reason: Test source covers numerical negative/above-one color vectors and browser readback, layer/mip/media/cleanup cases; GPU readback of extended-range HDR across supported backends is not established by the inspected tests. No tests were executed.

outcomes.description: clean source disposal
outcomes.reason: The source clears borrowed media, polling and CPU references after disposal listeners, without controlling the provider; the ledger records 125 focused source/mock tests before a later compiler type correction. The broader dynamic integration/typecheck remains pending, so this is source coverage only, not a current-candidate completion or acceptance claim.

outcomes.description: negotiated wide-gamut output
outcomes.reason: WebGL2 and WebGPU negotiate Display-P3, and WebGPU has a verified opaque full-screen output path plus an HDR tone route. Offscreen P3, direct-scene output, preserved alpha and additional post combinations remain unsupported.

outcomes.description: partial uploads
outcomes.reason: Device byte-range writes validate offsets and have source/mock coverage; the uniform-block path still uploads the whole block, so partial uploads across the wider shader-data scope are incomplete.

outcomes.description: mip generation/update
outcomes.reason: Explicit per-mip updates and WebGL generation exist; WebGPU generates source-image chains and render-target mips, but raw-data texture allocation uses the supplied mip count and lacks a corresponding automatic generation path.

outcomes.description: retained dynamic media/layer/mip updates
outcomes.reason: Video, layer and explicit mip changes have retained revision paths on the supported cases; updating a compressed texture through a decoded WebGPU fallback is explicitly rejected, and live media textures are restricted to flat 2D.
